meetings.title: Weekly Product Sync
meetings.overview: Weekly Product Sync covered onboarding funnel instrumentation, the mobile release candidate and the follow-up flow decision to group reminder emails. Maya owns the instrumentation PR, Daniel owns the release blocker triage, and Priya will map the V2 metrics against the Q3 OKR review scheduled for Thursday.
key_points: Onboarding drop-off is concentrated on the workspace-invite step: 38% of trial workspaces never invite a teammate.
The mobile release candidate 2.4.0 has passed internal QA; the crashing export path is the only blocker left.
Reminder emails will be batched to one daily digest instead of per-activity notifications.
Support tickets about duplicate transcripts dropped 22% after the retry change shipped last sprint.
Q3 OKR review is scheduled for Thursday and needs the activation metric definition locked first.

sections.title: Onboarding funnel
bullets: 38% of trial workspaces never reach the invite step; the drop is sharpest on mobile web.
Instrumentation PR will add step-level events so we can separate intent from friction.

sections.title: Release readiness
bullets: RC 2.4.0 passed internal QA on Tuesday; the export crash is the remaining blocker.
Daniel is triaging the crash today and will decide whether to cut 2.4.0 or ship 2.4.1.

sections.title: Notifications experiment
bullets: Per-activity reminder emails are being replaced by a single daily digest.
The digest will respect the workspace timezone setting that shipped last month.

sections.title: Metrics and Q3 review
bullets: Activation needs one agreed definition before the OKR review on Thursday.
Priya will map the existing V2 metrics sheet to the new definition.

action_items.title: Open the onboarding instrumentation PR with step-level events
Triage the mobile export crash and confirm the 2.4.0 release call
Draft the activation metric definition for the Q3 review
Update the support dashboard filter for duplicate transcripts
Share the digest copy with the customer success team

transcript.speaker: Aaron Kantor
transcript.text: Let's get started. I want to spend the first block on the onboarding funnel because the numbers look flat again this week.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Flat is generous. Trial workspaces that reach the invite step dropped from 46% to 38%, and almost all of that is mobile web.

transcript.speaker: Aaron Kantor
transcript.text: Do we know whether people are bouncing or just failing silently on that screen?

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: That's the problem, we cannot tell yet. The current events fire on the workspace creation, not on each onboarding step.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghunathan
transcript.text: I pulled the session recordings on Monday. Nine of twelve recordings show people tapping the invite field and nothing happening because autofill suggests a personal address.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: I'll open the instrumentation PR with step-level events so we can separate intent from friction. It should be up by Wednesday.

transcript.speaker: Aaron Kantor
transcript.text: Good. While that lands, how close are we on the mobile release candidate?

transcript.speaker: Daniel Okafor
transcript.text: RC 2.4.0 passed internal QA on Tuesday. The only blocker is the export crash on Android 15 when the transcript is longer than ten minutes.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Okafor
transcript.text: I'm triaging it today. If it's the chunked writer we can patch it in a point release, otherwise we cut 2.4.1 next week.

transcript.speaker: Aaron Kantor
transcript.text: Let's not hold the release for more than a day. A point release is acceptable if the fix is contained.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghunathan
transcript.text: Related note, support tickets about duplicate transcripts dropped 22% after the retry change shipped last sprint. That change is paying off.

transcript.speaker: Aaron Kantor
transcript.text: Nice. Now notifications, where did we land on the reminder emails?

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: The data says per-activity reminders are noise. We are going to group everything into a single daily digest that respects the workspace timezone.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Okafor
transcript.text: Can we make the digest opt-out per workspace rather than per user? Support gets nervous when notification settings change twice in a quarter.

transcript.speaker: Aaron Kantor
transcript.text: Agreed, workspace level first, per-user override later. I'll share the digest copy with the customer success team before we enable it.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghunathan
transcript.text: The Q3 OKR review is Thursday. We cannot present activation without one agreed definition of it.

transcript.speaker: Aaron Kantor
transcript.text: Right, that's the priority. Priya, can you map the existing V2 metrics sheet to a single activation definition?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghunathan
transcript.text: I'll draft the definition and flag the places where the current sheet disagrees with it. That should be ready for Thursday morning.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Once the definition is locked I can wire the dashboard to it, but not before Thursday.

transcript.speaker: Aaron Kantor
transcript.text: Perfect. Let's move on to release risks and then wrap with the support dashboard cleanup.

meetings.title: Design Review
meetings.overview: Design Review walked through the transcript notepad refresh and the empty-state illustrations. The team agreed to keep the two-panel notepad, replace the blue tint on active transcript rows with a purple wash, and ship the simplified share dialog. Rohan will prepare the motion spec and Elena will validate contrast in the dark sidebar.
key_points: The two-panel notepad layout stays; only spacing and the active row treatment change.
Active transcript rows will use a soft purple wash plus a left indicator instead of a solid tint.
The share dialog loses the permission matrix for launch and keeps the copy-link row.
Contrast in the dark sidebar fails AA on three secondary labels and needs new tokens.
Illustration set will be simplified to two variants to keep bundle size flat.

sections.title: Notepad refresh
bullets: Structural layout is validated; changes are limited to spacing and the active row treatment.
Mobile stacks the summary above the transcript with the player pinned.

sections.title: Share dialog
bullets: Permission matrix is deferred; copy-link stays in the first release.
Invite field gets a domain suggestion list once the API supports it.

sections.title: Accessibility pass
bullets: Three sidebar labels fall below 4.5:1 against the deep blue background.
Focus rings need a visible offset on the transcript list.

action_items.title: Prepare the motion spec for the active transcript row
Update sidebar tokens to pass AA contrast
Reduce the illustration set to two variants
Review the share dialog copy with support

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: The goal today is to close out the notepad refresh so engineering can start on Monday.

transcript.speaker: Rohan Iyer
transcript.text: Structurally the two-panel layout tested well. Everyone found the summary on the left and the transcript on the right without instructions.

transcript.speaker: Elena Petrova
transcript.text: The only confusion was the active row. The solid blue tint reads like a selection, so people expected a bulk action.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: So we replace it with a soft purple wash plus the left indicator bar. That matches the accent we already use for playback.

transcript.speaker: Rohan Iyer
transcript.text: I'll prepare the motion spec for that. The wash should fade in over 120 milliseconds, no easing bounce.

transcript.speaker: Elena Petrova
transcript.text: While we're in there, three sidebar labels fail contrast against the deep blue. The muted grey is too light.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Then we fix the tokens rather than the labels. Elena, can you update the sidebar tokens so everything passes AA?

transcript.speaker: Elena Petrova
transcript.text: Yes, I'll re-run the contrast audit and update the tokens. Two days is realistic.

transcript.speaker: Rohan Iyer
transcript.text: What about the share dialog? The permission matrix was in the last review.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: We decided to keep the copy-link row and defer the permission matrix. Nobody in testing understood group permissions anyway.

transcript.speaker: Elena Petrova
transcript.text: Agreed. The invite field should get domain suggestions later, but not in this release.

transcript.speaker: Rohan Iyer
transcript.text: Fine by me. I'll also reduce the illustration set to two variants so the bundle stays flat.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: One more thing, focus rings need an offset on the transcript list. Keyboard users lose the ring against the text.

transcript.speaker: Elena Petrova
transcript.text: I'll fold that into the accessibility pass with the sidebar tokens.

transcript.speaker: Rohan Iyer
transcript.text: Then we're done. I'll have the motion spec and the trimmed illustrations ready by Thursday.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: Great. Let's review the share dialog copy with support before we freeze strings.

meetings.title: Engineering Standup
meetings.overview: Engineering Standup focused on the transcript worker queue backlog, the flaky upload test and the decision to pin the Python runtime for the worker image. Sofia will drain the backlog with a batch size bump, Tom will stabilise the upload test, and the runtime pin ships today to unblock the container build.
key_points: Transcript worker backlog peaked at 240 jobs overnight and is draining at 80 jobs per hour.
Batch size can safely double because the queue depth is dominated by very short uploads.
The upload integration test is flaky because it asserts on wall-clock latency.
Worker container image will pin the Python runtime after the build broke twice this week.
No production incidents in the last seven days.

sections.title: Queue health
bullets: Backlog peaked at 240 jobs overnight; drain rate is 80 jobs per hour.
Batch size increases from 25 to 50 because jobs are mostly short uploads.

sections.title: Test stability
bullets: Upload integration test asserts wall-clock latency and fails under parallel load.
Tom will replace the timing assertion with a deterministic callback check.

sections.title: Container hygiene
bullets: Python runtime is pinned in the worker image to stop the base-image drift.
Image build moves to the same lockfile-driven step as the API service.

action_items.title: Raise the worker batch size and monitor the overnight backlog
Replace the wall-clock assertion in the upload test
Pin the Python runtime in the worker container image
Add a dashboard panel for queue drain rate

transcript.speaker: Daniel Okafor
transcript.text: Quick standup today. Sofia, you had the queue alert overnight, what happened?

transcript.speaker: Sofia Almeida
transcript.text: The transcript worker backlog peaked at 240 jobs around two in the morning. Nothing dropped, but we drained at 80 jobs per hour.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Okafor
transcript.text: Is the backlog depth coming from long recordings or from lots of tiny uploads?

transcript.speaker: Sofia Almeida
transcript.text: Mostly tiny uploads. Median job is under ninety seconds, so the per-job overhead is what hurts us.

transcript.speaker: Sofia Almeida
transcript.text: I'll raise the batch size from 25 to 50 and watch the backlog overnight. If the latency stays flat we keep it.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Okafor
transcript.text: Do it. I'd rather find the ceiling with a canary than guess. Tom, the upload test?

transcript.speaker: Tom Whitaker
transcript.text: It's still flaky. The test asserts on wall-clock latency, which is nonsense when the runner is under parallel load.

transcript.speaker: Maya Chen
transcript.text: That has failed three times this week and it always fails on the same assertion. Let's make it deterministic.

transcript.speaker: Tom Whitaker
transcript.text: Agreed, I'll replace the timing assertion with a callback check and mark the case as covered. Two days.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Okafor
transcript.text: Any production incidents since Friday?

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghunathan
transcript.text: None. Seven clean days. Error budget for the ingestion path is still above 90%.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Okafor
transcript.text: Last item, the worker image broke twice this week because the base image drifted. We're pinning the Python runtime today.

transcript.speaker: Sofia Almeida
transcript.text: Please also move the build to the same lockfile step as the API service so the two never disagree.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Okafor
transcript.text: Yes, same lockfile. I'll do that as part of the pin so we only touch the pipeline once.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghunathan
transcript.text: I'll add a dashboard panel for the queue drain rate so we catch the next backlog before it pages us.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Okafor
transcript.text: Perfect. That's standup, thanks everyone.

meetings.title: Customer Discovery Call — Northwind Labs
meetings.overview: Discovery call with Northwind Labs about their post-meeting workflow. Grace described a four-person operations team drowning in CRM follow-ups, and confirmed that searchable meeting transcripts with assignable action items would replace their current shared spreadsheet. Marcus flagged a security review requirement before any pilot, and Priya will send a scoped pilot proposal with SSO questions.
key_points: Northwind runs roughly 60 customer calls a month and every follow-up is manually copied into a spreadsheet.
The team loses about four hours a week re-listening to recordings to recover commitments.
Searchable transcripts with assignable action items would replace the spreadsheet entirely.
A security review covering retention and data residency is required before a pilot.
Pilot scope should cover the four-person operations team in one workspace.

sections.title: Current workflow
bullets: About 60 customer calls per month, each followed by a manual CRM update.
Four hours a week is spent re-listening to recordings to find commitments.

sections.title: What they need
bullets: Searchable transcripts so anyone can find the exact promise made on a call.
Action items that can be assigned to a teammate directly from the meeting.

sections.title: Security and pilot
bullets: Security review must confirm retention windows and data residency.
Pilot will start with the four-person operations team in a single workspace.

action_items.title: Send a scoped pilot proposal with retention options
Answer the Northwind security questionnaire
Map their CRM fields to our action item schema
Share the retention documentation folder

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghunathan
transcript.text: Thanks for making time. Before we show anything, tell me how your team handles follow-ups after a customer call.

transcript.speaker: Grace Lindqvist
transcript.text: Honestly it's a spreadsheet. Someone re-listens to the recording, types the commitments, then pastes them into the CRM.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Bell
transcript.text: We run about 60 customer calls a month across four people, so that spreadsheet has become a part-time job.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghunathan
transcript.text: How much time would you say goes into that recovery work every week?

transcript.speaker: Grace Lindqvist
transcript.text: Roughly four hours a week just to find what was actually promised. And we still miss things.

transcript.speaker: Aaron Kantor
transcript.text: When you miss something, what does that cost you?

transcript.speaker: Marcus Bell
transcript.text: Usually a renewal conversation that starts badly. Last quarter we lost a follow-up that was promised in a kickoff call.

transcript.speaker: Grace Lindqvist
transcript.text: What I actually want is to search a transcript and see the exact promise, then assign it to whoever owns the account.

transcript.speaker: Aaron Kantor
transcript.text: That's precisely what we're building. Would assignable action items replace the spreadsheet entirely?

transcript.speaker: Grace Lindqvist
transcript.text: Yes, if the assignments surface somewhere the team already looks. Email or Slack, not another tab.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Bell
transcript.text: Security is my concern. Anything that stores customer conversations needs a review of retention and data residency.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghunathan
transcript.text: Understood. I'll send the security questionnaire answers with the retention options so your review isn't blocked on us.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Bell
transcript.text: That would help a lot. Can you confirm whether transcripts can be deleted per meeting on request?

transcript.speaker: Aaron Kantor
transcript.text: Yes, deletion is per meeting and cascades to the notes and action items. I'll share the retention documentation folder today.

transcript.speaker: Grace Lindqvist
transcript.text: Then I'd like to pilot with the operations team first. Four people, one workspace, thirty days.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghunathan
transcript.text: That's a reasonable scope. I'll send a pilot proposal this week and Marcus, can you map your CRM fields to our action item schema?

transcript.speaker: Marcus Bell
transcript.text: I can do that. Send me a sample export and I'll match the fields.

transcript.speaker: Priya Raghunathan
transcript.text: Perfect. I'll include a sample with the proposal. Thank you both, this was really useful.

Transcript export moves to Sprint 25 because it depends on the renderer refactor.

meetings.title: Incident Review — Transcript Delay
meetings.overview: Incident review for the 42-minute transcript delay on the ingestion path. Root cause was a retry loop that amplified a slow storage call into a queue storm. The team agreed on exponential backoff with jitter, a circuit breaker on the storage client and a dedicated alert for queue age rather than queue depth. Tom will add the regression test and the postmortem will be shared with support.
key_points: Impact: transcripts were delayed up to 42 minutes for 310 meetings; no data was lost.
Root cause was a retry loop without backoff amplifying a slow storage call into a queue storm.
Fix: exponential backoff with jitter plus a circuit breaker on the storage client.
Alerting must watch queue age, not queue depth, because depth alone missed the incident.
Postmortem will be shared with support so first-line answers are consistent.

sections.title: Impact and timeline
bullets: 310 meetings delayed up to 42 minutes between 09:12 and 09:54.
Detection came from a customer report, not from monitoring.

sections.title: Root cause
bullets: A retry loop without backoff turned one slow storage call into thousands of retries.
Queue depth stayed inside its threshold, which is why the alert never fired.

sections.title: Follow-ups
bullets: Exponential backoff with jitter and a circuit breaker on the storage client.
New alert on queue age with a fifteen-minute page threshold.

action_items.title: Add exponential backoff with jitter to the storage client
Add an alert on queue age with a 15 minute threshold
Write a regression test for the retry storm
Share the postmortem with the support team

transcript.speaker: Sofia Almeida
transcript.text: This is a blameless review of the transcript delay yesterday morning. Tom, you were on call, can you walk the timeline?

transcript.speaker: Tom Whitaker
transcript.text: At 09:12 the ingestion path slowed. By 09:20 the queue had thousands of pending retries and transcripts were arriving up to 42 minutes late.

transcript.speaker: Tom Whitaker
transcript.text: We heard about it from a customer at 09:38, which is the part that bothers me most, because our own alerts never fired.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Okafor
transcript.text: I cleared it by 09:54 when I drained the retry backlog and the storage call recovered. Nothing was lost, 310 meetings were delayed.

transcript.speaker: Sofia Almeida
transcript.text: Let's talk about the cause. What actually triggered the storm?

transcript.speaker: Daniel Okafor
transcript.text: A single slow storage call. The client retried immediately with no backoff, so each retry spawned more work. It was a self-inflicted amplification.

transcript.speaker: Tom Whitaker
transcript.text: And the queue depth metric stayed inside its threshold the whole time, because jobs were being picked up, just not finished.

transcript.speaker: Sofia Almeida
transcript.text: So our alert was measuring the wrong thing. Queue depth said healthy while queue age was screaming.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Okafor
transcript.text: Exactly. I'll add exponential backoff with jitter to the storage client and put a circuit breaker in front of it.

transcript.speaker: Sofia Almeida
transcript.text: I'll add an alert on queue age with a fifteen minute page threshold. That would have fired at 09:15.

transcript.speaker: Tom Whitaker
transcript.text: I'll write a regression test that simulates the slow storage call and asserts we stop retrying. Without that, the backoff will get removed by someone in six months.

transcript.speaker: Sofia Almeida
transcript.text: Good. Two more things: the postmortem goes to support so first-line answers are consistent, and we add this scenario to the runbook.

transcript.speaker: Daniel Okafor
transcript.text: Should we also cap total retries? A hard ceiling would have bounded the blast radius regardless of backoff.

transcript.speaker: Sofia Almeida
transcript.text: Yes, ceiling plus backoff. I don't want one failure mode to depend on a single mitigation.

transcript.speaker: Tom Whitaker
transcript.text: Agreed. That's everything from my side.

transcript.speaker: Sofia Almeida
transcript.text: Thanks both. Postmortem is written, I'll share it with support and we close the follow-ups next week.
